findings.body:
**Validate every `default_branch` component.**

At `apps/crq-python/repo_registry.py:72`, `release.lock/main` and `release/.hidden/main` pass validation. Git prohibits a component that ends with `.lock` or starts with `.`. Neither generated `default_ref` can identify the reference that `push_current.py:311-312` resolves. Validate each component before returning the configuration. Keep `main` and `release/main` valid. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ref-format/2.12.5?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Validate every `defaultbranch` component.

findings.body:
**Accept valid Git branch names in `default_branch`.**

`BRANCH` at `apps/crq-python/repo_registry.py:16` requires an ASCII alphanumeric first and last character. `parse_entry` refuses any other value with `invalid default_branch` (lines 70-73). Git accepts names such as `_staging` and `release-`, and the design note in `apps/crq-python/docs/multi-repo.md` does not restrict branch syntax. A configured repository with such a default branch makes `repo_registry.parse` raise `ValueError` during `apps/crq-python/crq.py:90`. That module-level call has no guard, so the import fails.

Validate `default_branch` against Git's ref-name rules instead. Keep the existing rejections in `apps/crq-python/test_repo_registry.py:86-89` (`-main`, `a..b`, `a//b`, `refs.lock`). Add accepting cases for `_staging` and `release-`. No code patch is proposed here because the exact rule set is a policy choice.
findings.title: Accept valid Git branch names in `defaultbranch`.

findings.body:
**Change only the final source manifest in this test.**

`copy.deepcopy(phases_value)` preserves the shared `source` references inside the copy. This assignment changes the guest digest in `prepare` and every other phase as well as `partial-inspect`. A verifier that checks only `prepare` can still emit the expected `source manifest` diagnostic.

Replace the `partial-inspect` source dictionary with a copy containing the wrong digest. Keep the prepared manifest valid so rejection depends on the final manifest.
findings.title: Change only the final source manifest in this test.

findings.body:
**Keep completion accumulation local to one evidence build.**

`evidence()` leaves the final completion list on `self`. In the mutation loop at Line 2760, the next call starts with the previous build’s activation completions already in its install baseline. The subtests therefore change the starting log as well as the selected recovery field.

Start each build from the same baseline and advance a local list across its cases. This preserves append-only history within each build without carrying history into the next subtest.
findings.title: Keep completion accumulation local to one evidence build.

findings.body:
**Test each process-preservation check separately.**

This test marks both processes dead before calling the verifier. If the verifier stops checking the owned process but still checks the unrelated process, the test passes. The reverse is also true. Use a fresh fixture for each mutation so either missing check fails its own subtest.
findings.title: Test each process-preservation check separately.

findings.body:
**Keep the before and after snapshots independent.**

At Line 186, `dict(quiet)` copies only the outer dictionary. When Line 883 changes the after snapshot’s symlink target, it also changes the before snapshot’s target. The test can then pass because the metadata contradicts the file inventory, not because the target changed across the refusal.

Build `after` with a second `observation()` call. The positive control will still start with equal snapshots.
findings.title: Keep the before and after snapshots independent.
